title: HPE launches four new AMD-powered servers as part of its ProLiant Gen13 portfolio
key_facts: HPE announced the first four ProLiant Gen13 servers, all running 6th Gen AMD EPYC (Venice) processors.

The four are the DL585a Gen13 (two-socket, up to eight double-wide GPUs), the DL525 Gen13 (1U single-socket, up to 256 cores, the first of the four to ship), and the XD245 and XD285 Gen13 dense-compute systems.
All four carry PCIe Gen6 and a new iLO 8 management processor.
HPE's John Carter, vice president of mainstream compute, said the launch is aimed at agentic AI, EDA, CAE and simulation.
HPE's release says Gen13 will expand to mainstream enterprise servers after these four; asked about a mainstream two-socket 2U model, Carter said it is not available today.
HPE's product brief claims up to 2x compute performance without naming the comparison system.
quote_evidence: HPE has announced the first four ProLiant Gen13 servers, and all of them run on 6th Gen AMD EPYC, the SP7-socket Venice parts AMD listed last month.
Asked about a mainstream two-socket 2U Gen13 server, Carter said: “not today, but stay tuned.”
The product brief claims up to 2x the compute performance without naming the comparison system, and notes that direct liquid cooling is optional for denser configurations.
why_it_matters_hint: New AMD-based servers for AI and engineering work are launching now, with mainstream models to follow later.
